The opening statement and displayed leakage asymptotics already had the right direction. Independently, conditional averaging divides the position variance by N, and division by (2a)² gives t_N. The angular log derivative is strictly increasing with opposite infinite ends, hence the latent density is U-shaped. Endpoint ramps have derivative signs +,-,+,-, converge in L¹, and give the at-most-three sign changes by Gaussian variation diminution. The semigroup makes the mode count nonincreasing. All critical points lie inside (−1,1); strict posterior log-concavity at t=1 and compactness preserve a unique mode slightly below it. Signs witnessing two strict maxima persist in t; they exist for small t by the two nondegenerate scaled edge peaks, hence there is exactly one separating t_c in (0,1). At t_c a degenerate critical point is required since a finite set of simple critical points in the compact region would persist. The scale change z=1−√t s gives the t^−1/4 density profile; integration by parts on s^(1/2) times the Gaussian gives F″+ξF′+F/2=0. F vanishes at both infinities and every zero of F′ is a strict maximum; F′(0)<0 and differentiable local convergence thus locate both inward peaks and their heights. The mirrored integrations give the two t^1/4 leakages, and Tonelli gives C=2∫₀^∞ uφ₁(u)/√u du=2^(1/4)Γ(3/4)/√π. Both surviving right/left ratios are A_+/A_-=cosh(πλ).
